SPECIAL MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
MONDAY - SEPTEMBER 13, 2021 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
* COVID-19 NOTICE *
To protect public health and safety during the COVID-19 pandemic and in compliance with the current Los Angeles County Health Officer Order and City of Cerritos COVID-19 Safety Plan, the City Council Chamber will be open to the public. As authorized by State of California Executive Orders N-25-20, N-29-20, and N-08-21, and subsequently by Assembly Bill 361 (Chapter 165, Statutes of 2021), this meeting may also be conducted via teleconference, if necessary. Public observation and participation in this meeting will be facilitated through the methods described below.
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in-person in the Council Chamber subject to posted COVID-19 protocols.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in-person at the meeting or by using the following alternate methods:
Written correspondence (hard copy or email): Public comments can be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting. During the meeting, your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

This section is reserved for comments related to the Consent Calendar, Closed Session, and/or items not listed on the agenda but that are within the subject matter jurisdiction of the legislative body. Comments are limited to 5 minutes per person.
7.
Consent Calendar
Items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by one motion. Subject to the discretion of the legislative body, there will be no separate discussion of these items unless a legislative body member or citizen so requests, in which event the item may be removed from the Consent Calendar and considered separately.

Thursday, August 26, 2021, 7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

11A.
Report from City Manager/Executive Director
During this part of the meeting the City Manager/Executive Director or designated staff will have an opportunity to report on various City matters and/or respond verbally to questions or comments from the prior City Council meeting, including any request by the City Council to provide a brief supplemental report or brief follow-up response to items from the prior City Council meeting's agenda.
11B.
City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Meeting Reports
During this part of the meeting members of the City Council report to the community on various matters of interest, including reports concerning committees on which the Councilmembers serve and reports on meetings/conferences attended. In addition, requests may be made of the staff for reports which will be presented to the City Council at a subsequent meeting, or for the scheduling of future agenda items. There will be no discussion or action taken on any of the items that may be presented during this agenda item.

Closed Session Report
After the City Council/Successor Agency reconvenes into Open Session, designated City staff will provide a verbal report on any reportable action taken in Closed Session. This report will be memorialized in the official meeting minutes.
13.

MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD MONDAY,
SEPTEMBER 13, 2021, 7:00 P.M., IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL,
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA.

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Boy Scout Troop 72.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Bruce Barrows
  Council/Agency Member Naresh Solanki
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Chuong Vo
  Mayor/Chair Grace Hu

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5A.  Presentations

  None.

5B.  Informational update on the City's response to the COVID-19 pandemic and other City
  events, services, and programs.

  An informational report was given by Annie Hylton, City Librarian & Marketing Manager. A
  PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  There was no further action taken on this item.

MOTION TO ADD ITEM TO A FUTURE AGENDA: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Solanki, to
direct the City Manager to place an agenda report regarding review and consideration of continuation of
the Fine Arts and Historical Commission on the next City Council/Successor Agency meeting agenda
where all members of the City Council/Successor Agency are scheduled to be present
(COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

AYES:  Barrows, Solanki, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None
ABSTAIN:  None

5.  Presentations/Appointments (continued)

5C.  Review and consideration of City Council appointments to fill vacancies for unexpired terms
  on the Cerritos Advisory Boards (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer.

  Councilmember Solanki offered his nomination of Pinal Doshi to fill the unscheduled
  vacancy on the Community Safety Committee. He stated he would defer his nomination to
  fill the unscheduled vacancy on the Fine Arts and Historical Committee to a future City
  Council meeting.

  Councilmember Yokoyama stated he would defer his nomination to the Community Safety
  Committee to a future City Council meeting.

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Barrows, to approve the appointment of
  Councilmember Solanki’s nomination of the following individual from the established eligibility
  list to fill an unexpired term ending April 30, 2022 on the City’s Advisory Boards, as follows:

  Advisory Board  Name
  Community Safety Committee  Pinal Doshi

  (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Solanki, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  The aforementioned action creates an unscheduled vacancy on the Let Freedom Ring
  Committee and a notice to fill the unscheduled vacancy will be posted in compliance with
  the requirements of California Government Code Section 54974.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Written correspondence:
  (Written correspondence is considered public record and full-text copies of submitted
  written correspondence can be obtained in the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer)

  Marsha Miller submitted written correspondence in support of sponsoring programs to
  assist Afghan refugees.

  Sue Carter submitted written correspondence requesting the City Council revisit the
  request from CalMet Services for an adjustment to the maximum allowable solid waste
  management rates.

  In-person public comments:

  Nancy Gutzmer, representing the American Cancer Society, spoke in support of the
  upcoming Relay for Life event.

  Emely Merina spoke in support of the upcoming Relay for Life event.

  Marsha Miller spoke in support of sponsoring programs to assist Afghan refugees.

City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting  Page 3 of 10

  Katherine George Chu spoke in opposition to a panelist invited to speak at a Cerritos
  Republican Club event at the Cerritos Library.

  Seth Grossman spoke in opposition to a panelist invited to speak at a Cerritos Republican

  Sam Desai spoke in opposition to a panelist invited to speak at a Cerritos Republican Club

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7D.  Award of contract for the Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts mailing list data
  processing services, RFP No. 1433-21 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Solanki, to:

  1. Award a contract for Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts mailing list data processing
  services, RFP No. 1433-21, to Carney Direct Marketing, with the following provisions:

  a. The term of the contract shall begin upon the City Council’s award of bid and
  extends for 18 months; and
  b. The term of the agreement may be extended by mutual agreement of both parties
  for up to 3 additional 12-month terms; and
  c. Upon completion of the 18-month period of the agreement, the data processing
  services firm may request that the City approve an increase in the project fees for
  work to be completed for the additional period. Such requests for increase shall be
  based on the Consumer Price Index for the Bureau of Labor Statistics, U.S.
  Department of Labor, Los Angeles – Long Beach metropolitan area for the period of
  July 1 through June 30 of the calendar year immediately preceding the date of such
  adjustment. The maximum increase for any period shall be 3 percent (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Solanki, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7E.  Award of single source purchase for the procurement of carpet for the multimedia area
  within the Cerritos Library (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Solanki, to:

  1. Make a finding that staff has satisfied the purpose of the bidding statute of the Cerritos
  Municipal Code, and that it is reasonable and necessary to single source purchase the
  custom-designed carpet for the Cerritos Library’s Multimedia Area from Brintons (the
  supplier) to maintain the unique Art Deco design and theme; and

  2. Approve the appropriation and expenditure of funds in the amount of $30,000 from
  Capital Improvement Project 22203 for the expenditure; and

  3. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to approve any change orders that may
  become necessary to complete the subject purchase (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Solanki, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

(minutes continue on the next page)

8.  Public Hearings

8A.  Review and consideration of final proposed sites to be included in the City of Cerritos 2021-
  2029 Housing Element for potential reuse as housing, and an update regarding the status
  of the City’s preparation of its 2021-2029 Housing Element (COUNCIL).

  Staff reports were given by Kristin Aguila, Advance Planning Manager, Torrey Contreras,
  Senior Assistant City Manager, Diane Bathgate, RRM Consulting, and Brady Woods, RRM
  Consulting. A PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments period.

  Written correspondence:
  (Written correspondence is considered public record and full-text copies of submitted
  written correspondence can be obtained in the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer)

  The following individuals submitted written correspondence related to various aspects of
  the proposed sites to be included in the City of Cerritos 2021-2029 Housing Element:

  Nancy Davis
  Nondra Pang
  Mark Martinez
  Nazeef Kazi
  Sarah (last name not provided)
  Anita Dharma
  Marty and Kristen Knowles
  Linda Cecola
  Brenda Gutierrez
  Sharon Thornburg
  Jiayuann Du
  Kun-Jer Lee

  In-person public comments:

  Rod Dixon spoke in opposition to many of the proposed sites to be included in the City of
  Cerritos 2021-2029 Housing Element citing congestion and other negative impacts to the
  adjacent neighborhoods. He spoke in support of Site 7 and the former Sears building site.

  Judi Dixon spoke in opposition to many of the proposed sites to be included in the City of
  Cerritos 2021-2029 Housing Element citing congestion and other negative impacts to the
  adjacent neighborhoods. She spoke in support of Site 7 and the former Sears building site.

  Richard Lee requested the City Council withdraw Site 4 from the list of proposed sites to be
  included in the City of Cerritos 2021-2029 Housing Element.

  James Kang inquired whether including a proposed site in the Housing Element is an initial
  step toward eminent domain proceedings and requested the City Council withdraw Site 4
  from the list of proposed sites to be included in the City of Cerritos 2021-2029 Housing
  Element.

  Justin Chue requested the City Council withdraw Site 4 from the list of proposed sites to be
  included in the City of Cerritos 2021-2029 Housing Element.

  Poom Sirinirund requested the City Council withdraw Site 4 from the list of proposed sites
  to be included in the City of Cerritos 2021-2029 Housing Element.
 City of Cerritos  Monday, September 13, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting  Page 7 of 10

8.  Public Hearings (continued)

8A.  (continued)

  Amy Kelly requested the City Council withdraw Site 3 from the list of proposed sites to be
  included in the City of Cerritos 2021-2029 Housing Element citing traffic and other negative
  impacts to the adjacent neighborhoods.

  Sylvester Ani inquired whether the declining enrollments in ABCUSD are utilized as a factor
  in determining the required number of low-income property units and whether the required
  number of units is an unfunded State mandate.

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to provide public comment, the Mayor
  declared the public comments period and public hearing closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to direct staff to:

  1. Finalize the City’s draft 2021-2029 Housing Element document to include:

  a. Sites 1, 7, 8, A, and B, as identified in the subject agenda report for this item, with
  an increase in the density for site 7 and distribution of any additional increases in
  density across the remaining sites 1, 8, A, and B if appropriate.
  b. Income category designations and density designations discussed in the official
  agenda report for this item.

  2. Release the finalized draft 2021-2029 Housing Element document for public review and
  comment; and

  3. Submit the finalized draft document to the State of California Department of Housing
  and Community Development for review and comment (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Solanki, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu
